title: Jonah and the Cipher
premise: Mara Ishikawa has spent a decade as the night dispatcher for Calloway Cabs, the town's unofficial archive of secrets — until a prepaid fare named Elias Vann asks her to prove that councilman Aldous Reeve will not be murdered on the anniversary of his wife's drowning. Digging through ten years of dispatch logs, Mara discovers that the 'closed' case of Lena Reeve's death was closed by someone with access to the same records she keeps. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Mara realizes the murder hasn't happened yet because the killer is still waiting — and that her own late father's handwriting appears in the oldest logbook. In the end, Mara exposes that Aldous Reeve killed his wife and has been paying the taxi company itself to bury the evidence; she chooses to break her father's code of silence, testifying at the anniversary dinner where Reeve planned to announce his candidacy, trading her invisibility for the truth.
about_author: Elodie Okafor is a former municipal archivist who spent six years cataloguing small-town court records before turning to fiction full-time. She writes mysteries about the people who keep a town's paperwork — and what the paperwork keeps about them.

chapters.title: The Night Book
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A quiet shift establishes Calloway Cabs as the town's confessional: drunks confess, widows reminisce, and Mara files it all in coded logbooks her father invented. Emotional beat: comfortable invisibility, faintly lonely. The chapter ends when a stranger walks in at 3 a.m. and pays a year's fares in advance.

chapters.title: Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Elias Vann hires her not for a ride but for a task: prove that Aldous Reeve won't be murdered at next month's anniversary dinner. He offers no reason, only cash and a deadline. Beat: wary curiosity. Mara almost refuses, but Vann mentions her father's name, and she can't let that go.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She pulls the dispatch logs from the night Lena Reeve drowned, expecting routine entries, and finds a two-hour gap — pages cut out cleanly. Beat: first real unease. Her boss, Denny Calloway, catches her in the archive and tells her some books stay shut, revealing he knows more than he should.

chapters.title: The Widow's Table
chapters.summary: Alternate POV: Deputy Cora Lin, who signed off on the drowning verdict a decade ago. Cora remembers pressure from above to close the case fast, and a taxi waiting outside the Reeve house that never appeared in any report. Beat: guilt resurfacing. She begins quietly re-reading her own old notes.

chapters.title: Cipher of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Decoding her father's margin shorthand, she finds recurring pickups from the Reeve boathouse logged under a false account name — one her father created. Beat: betrayal and grief braided together. She realizes her father didn't just record the town's secrets; he was paid to curate them.

chapters.title: What Vann Knows
chapters.summary: Mara confronts Elias Vann at a diner. He admits he was Lena Reeve's brother, estranged, and received an anonymous letter last month claiming Aldous plans to kill again — this time a witness. Beat: reluctant alliance. Mara agrees to help, telling herself it's about the gap in the logbook, not the letter.

chapters.title: Denny's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She breaks into the office safe and finds Denny's private ledger: annual payments from the Reeve estate, dated every year since the drowning, including one deposited last week. Beat: dread crystallizing. The payments weren't hush money for the past — they were retainers for something still pending.

chapters.title: Cora's Cold File
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. In the evidence locker, Cora discovers Lena's autopsy photo shows bruising inconsistent with drowning, and that the file was re-ordered by someone with administrative access — the signature trail leads toward the mayor's office. Beat: professional shame turning to resolve. She photographs everything.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The dinner's seating chart surfaces through a catering order dispatched by cab: forty guests, including Vann, Cora, and Mara herself, invited under a name she doesn't recognize. Beat: paranoia blooming. Someone has been orchestrating the guest list for weeks — and it wasn't Aldous.

chapters.title: Ghost Account
chapters.summary: Mara traces the false boathouse account to its creator date: three days before Lena died, opened by her father. Flashback chapter told partly in his voice through marginalia. Beat: mourning. Mara understands her father tried to leave a trail for whoever came after him — and that trail points to the dinner.

chapters.title: Threat Assessment
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. Vann admits the anonymous letter named him as the future victim, and that he came to Mara because her father once promised Lena protection he failed to give. Beat: vulnerability beneath calculation. Vann reveals he's already hired no one else — Mara is his entire plan, which terrifies them both.

chapters.title: Cut Pages
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She reconstructs the missing logbook hours from radio archives and driver memory, placing a second car at the boathouse the night Lena died — driven by a young Denny Calloway. Beat: anger hardening into purpose. When she confronts Denny, he doesn't deny it; he warns her the payments bought silence, not crime.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. Cora receives the same anonymous letter Vann got, postmarked locally, and recognizes the typewriter ribbon impression from cold cases she handled. Beat: the hunter realizing she's bait. She sets a trap at the post office and glimpses the sender — someone she thought was dead.

chapters.title: Lena's Sister
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The sender is revealed: Ruth, Lena's other sibling, presumed gone for a decade, who has been living in town under a false name — as the caterer for the anniversary dinner. Beat: vertigo. Ruth claims she isn't threatening anyone; she's counting down to a public reckoning, and the letters were invitations.

chapters.title: Retainer
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny explains the arrangement: after Lena's death, Aldous paid the company to control every record, route, and witness near the boathouse, and Denny kept the system running out of fear and complicity. Beat: confession without absolution. He hands Mara the original unciphered master log and tells her to decide what the town deserves.

chapters.title: Forty Covers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Two days before the dinner, Mara maps every guest against the logs and finds the pattern: each attendee is connected to a piece of evidence Aldous believes destroyed. Beat: rising dread. The dinner isn't a celebration or a murder — it's Aldous auditing his own cover-up before announcing his candidacy.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Revisited
chapters.summary: Cora and Mara, dual POV sections. They search the rebuilt boathouse and find Lena's original personal effects hidden in a wall cavity — including a diary naming her husband and describing the 'kind man who drives the night cab' who promised to help her leave. Beat: heartbreak. Her father was her escape plan, and he arrived too late.

chapters.title: Countdown Dinner
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The anniversary dinner begins. Toasts are raised, Aldous takes the podium, and Mara watches Vann, Ruth, and Cora take their seats like pieces on a board. Beat: coiled tension. Mara slips the reconstructed logbook pages into the place settings just as Aldous begins his announcement.

chapters.title: What Hasn't Happened Yet
chapters.summary: Climax, Mara's POV. Aldous, seeing the pages circulate, abandons the speech and goes for Ruth in the kitchen; Vann intervenes, Cora arrests him on decade-old evidence now corroborated, and Denny arrives to surrender the master ledger voluntarily. Beat: explosive release. The murder that hadn't happened yet was always the one Aldous committed ten years ago.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Cora's POV. The reopening of the case, depositions, and the town's reckoning — neighbors who suspected, drivers who drove, officials who looked away. Beat: sober catharsis. Cora formally amends her decade-old ruling, and Mara gives testimony that names her father's complicity alongside his courage.

chapters.title: Closing the Logbook
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Aftermath: Denny retires and offers Mara the company; she declines, taking instead the complete archive to donate to the county historical society, unredacted. Beat: quiet transformation. Vann leaves town, but first pays one final fare — a ride to the cemetery, which Mara drives herself.

chapters.title: First Morning Shift
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Months later, Mara works days now, training a new dispatcher on honest logbooks, when a stranger asks to pay in advance for a job. Beat: earned peace with vigilance. She smiles, opens a fresh ledger, and says: 'Tell me the truth first. Then we'll see what it costs.'
